The original observer host adds viewport/background/environment and fixture controls, with no parent opacity, overlay or button-style substitution. Thus the supported cause is the component disabled rendering, not a host-region sample or an unsuitable/missing observation. The precise framework alpha mechanism is inferred rather than instrumented; the attribution rests on the actual component-owned surface, matching native box, coherent state and visible original evidence.

The original PNG shows the dimmed actual disabled primary button, not outer host background or an overlaid child. The approved bridge only decodes the model/maps callbacks and does not repaint the button. Enabled states render the intended enabled fill. The likely mechanism is default button-style disabled opacity; exact internal SwiftUI compositing is inferred, while component ownership and the rendered mismatch are directly evidenced.

judge_one.reason: The unchanged original plan explicitly expected #FFAAA99F ARGB on workshop.submit in this exact P1/ios/replaced state. Original artifact and plan match the transport and SHA. Direct inspection of every cited original screenshot shows the disabled primary button. Frozen native_pixels recomputation measures #FFCFCDC5 in the approved solid side strip inside the unique, fully visible, disabled submit semantic box, with consistent native state binding. This is the specific original color finding, and the same exact row is failed/product in common D0. No later state or repair supplies detection support.

judge_two.reason: Original failed native_pixels assertion explicitly identifies this exact state and primary fill. Original plan expected 4289374623 with unit argb is unchanged. Inspection of its original PNGs and native facts confirms a unique fully visible disabled workshop.submit; direct re-sampling of the original approved glyph-free strip has 100% support for opaque #CFCDC5, contradicting #AAA99F. Frozen candidate-v8 re-evaluation on the unchanged original plan/own-D0 observation reproduces the same failed assertion and cited snapshots. Common D0 independently marks this exact row failed with product cause. Support is restricted to this one original scope key; FINAL repair was not used as detection proof.

WorkshopSlotPlanner.swift paints palette.disabled in its label and applies PlainButtonStyle() plus .disabled(selected == nil) to the enclosing button. Its palette declares the approved opaque light/dark disabled colors. Direct original and common-D0 screenshots and frozen sampling reproduce #FFCFCDC5 versus #FFAAA99F in light, and #FF33474C versus #FF52666A in dark. The approved observer host supplies background, viewport and environment without an opacity/overlay/button-style substitution; the bridge only maps fixtures and callbacks. Thus these four correlated manifestations share the same disabled component rendering cause, rather than independent defects per state/theme. The exact internal SwiftUI alpha mechanism is inferred, but common source path, ownership and manifestation membership are directly supported. No Android row is in the confirmed product universe.

Original raw pixel strips reproduce #CFCDC5 rather than #AAA99F in P1 and #33474C rather than #52666A in P2. Enabled states do not belong to the failed universe.
